issues.legal_issue: Property inherited from paternal ancestors is ancestral only in relation to the holder’s male issue and is separate property in relation to other heirs when the holder leaves no male issue.
material_facts: The disputed properties had originally belonged to the deceased holder’s paternal ancestors.
The deceased was the last male holder and left no male issue.
No surviving member of a joint family could take the properties by survivorship.
The competing claimants were paternal collaterals and the claimant was the deceased’s sister.

For purposes of deciding the case, the court proceeded on the basis that the applicable custom preferred collaterals to a sister only for ancestral property, and preferred a sister to collaterals for non-ancestral property.
issues.conclusion: As against the paternal collaterals, the properties were not ancestral property; the sister was the preferential heir and was entitled to all the disputed properties.
issues.legal_principle: Property inherited from paternal ancestors is ancestral as regards the holder’s male issue, but is the holder’s absolute property as regards other relations. If the holder dies without male issue, the property passes by succession as separate property in relation to those other relations. The court relied on Mulla, Principles of Hindu Law, 15th ed., pp. 289 and 291, and applied the assumed custom distinguishing the heirs to ancestral and non-ancestral property.

rule.if: inheritance_dispute and property_inherited_from_paternal_ancestors and holder_left_no_male_issue and no_surviving_joint_family_member_can_take_by_survivorship and claimant_is_sister and competing_claimants_are_paternal_collaterals and custom_prefers_sister_for_non_ancestral_property

predicates.inheritance_dispute: The dispute concerns who inherits property from a deceased holder.
predicates.property_inherited_from_paternal_ancesto: The holder acquired the disputed property by inheritance from paternal ancestors.
predicates.holder_left_no_male_issue: The holder died without leaving male issue.
predicates.no_surviving_joint_family_member_can_tak: No surviving joint-family member could take the property by survivorship.
predicates.claimant_is_sister: The person claiming inheritance is the deceased holder’s sister.
predicates.competing_claimants_are_paternal_collate: The competing claimants are paternal collateral relatives of the deceased holder.
predicates.custom_prefers_sister_for_non_ancestral_: The applicable custom gives a sister preference over paternal collaterals for property that is non-ancestral in relation to them.

issues.definition: When inherited paternal property is disputed between a sister and paternal collaterals, the holder left no male issue, and no joint-family member could take by survivorship, the sister is the preferential heir if the applicable custom prefers her for non-ancestral property.

issues.legal_issue: A procedural technicality should not prevent an appeal from being considered on its merits when the appeal was timely or had already been admitted.
material_facts: The first appeal was admitted and was later dismissed because the appellant had not personally presented the memorandum of appeal.
The second appeal was filed within the limitation period, but a copy of the trial court’s judgment was filed after that period expired.
The courts below dismissed the appeals on those procedural grounds rather than deciding the merits.
issues.conclusion: The dismissals were erroneous; the delay in filing the copy should have been condoned, the appeals should have been considered on their merits, and the judgments dismissing them were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Rules of procedure are intended to advance the cause of justice, not to short-circuit a decision on the merits. The court held that an appeal already admitted should not later be dismissed for the stated personal-presentation defect, and that delay in filing a copy of the trial court’s judgment should have been condoned where the second appeal itself was filed in time.

predicates.civil_appeal_proceeding: The matter is a civil appeal proceeding.
predicates.admitted_first_appeal_dismissed_for_pers: A first appeal was admitted and was later dismissed because the appellant did not personally present the appeal memorandum.
predicates.timely_second_appeal_with_late_judgment_: A second appeal was filed within the applicable time, but the copy of the lower court’s judgment was filed later.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal proceeding, when either an admitted first appeal is dismissed for a personal-presentation defect or a timely second appeal has a late-filed judgment copy, the procedural dismissal should be set aside and the merits considered.
